children: The roughly 42,000 drop in Canadian employment in August is likely a labor-supply story, reflecting flat population growth, says Ali Jaffery, KPMG Canada's chief economist. Jaffery says the level of unemployment increased slightly in August, up 4,800, whereas the labor force contracted 37,000. "That size of a 'swing' in the labour force has become normal in this low-population growth economy," Jaffery says. Canada's population is estimated to have edged downward 0.1% in 2Q from the prior 3-month period, part of an attempt by Ottawa to limit immigration after years of fast growth.
